headline: Deep learning links peptide sequence and structure to antimicrobial function
label: Deep Learning Peptide Prediction
summary: Protein language model embeddings and structure-aware architectures now target generation and interaction-level prediction, not only sequence classification.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning applied to peptide and protein sequences, with protein language model embeddings or multi-view sequence and structure features as the representational core. KEMP-PIP fuses ESM embeddings with k-mer and physicochemical features for pro-inflammatory peptide prediction, and PeptideNet pairs ESM1, ESM2 and ProtBert embeddings with CNN-BiGRU models for five bioactive peptide classes. Antimicrobial work spans classification and design: MultiAMP integrates sequence and structure at multiple scales, a dual diffusion framework fuses peptide sequence and structure with contrastive learning for classification, and PLUM organizes a conditional VAE latent space by function, length and sequence context for controlled generation. CrossAffinity predicts protein-protein binding affinity from sequence alone using cross-attention, and BIN-PU addresses bacterial compound-protein interactions using only positive samples via positive-unlabeled learning. What is new relative to sequence-only classifiers is the spread toward generative, interaction-level and structure-aware prediction, while a uniform design study addresses tetra-peptide physicochemical properties.
